eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Paris’s August 1, 2026, daily maximum temperature centers on 28 °C and 29 °C because the latest ensemble forecasts converge on those values.** Official guidance, including the UK Met Office run issued July 31, projects a daytime high of 29 °C under mostly clear skies with overnight lows near 18 °C. Météo-France and other numerical weather prediction centers show similar consensus, with only modest spread around 28–29 °C and negligible probability mass above 30 °C or below 27 °C.

Atmospheric conditions supporting this narrow range include a building but not yet extreme high-pressure ridge over western Europe that favors subsidence and solar heating without strong advection of hotter continental air. Paris’s urban heat-island effect adds 1–2 °C to regional maxima on calm, sunny days, helping anchor the forecast near the upper end of seasonal norms (climatological August highs average ~25–26 °C). Recent model runs have shown only minor adjustments, keeping 28–29 °C as the mode and explaining the combined 99.5 % market-implied probability for those two outcomes.

Upcoming official bulletins from Météo-France and any rapid-update high-resolution models will be the next potential catalysts if they shift the consensus by even 1 °C.
